behavior: Quiet keeps every config pair the environment already carries and appends its own after them, so both the caller's keys and Quiet's apply — including where the caller pins the same key to the opposite value, and where it pins the key twice and so ends on a value Quiet must still outrank: the two cases where precedence is observable.
verification:
cd cli && out="$(go test ./internal/gittest -run '^(TestQuietKeepsTheCallersConfig|TestQuietAppendsAfterAForeignEnvironment|TestQuietOutranksAConflictingCallerPair|TestQuietOutranksACallerThatSetsTheSameKeyTwice)$' -v -count=1)" && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietKeepsTheCallersConfig' && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietAppendsAfterAForeignEnvironment' && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietOutranksAConflictingCallerPair' && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietOutranksACallerThatSetsTheSameKeyTwice'

behavior: A second Quiet call in a re-executed test binary adds nothing: no duplicate pairs and no nested system config.
verification: cd cli && out="$(go test ./internal/gittest -run '^(TestQuietAcceptsItsOwnKeys|TestQuietDoesNotIncludeItsOwnFile)$' -v -count=1)" && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietAcceptsItsOwnKeys' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietDoesNotIncludeItsOwnFile'

behavior: The refusals that must survive still panic — a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, a count promising a pair the environment does not carry, a count too large to be real, and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM — and a refused call leaves the environment as it found it.
verification:
cd cli && out="$(go test ./internal/gittest -run '^(TestQuietRefusesAMalformedCount|TestQuietRefusesBeforeItTouchesTheEnvironment|TestQuietRefusesNoSystem)$' -v -count=1)" && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietRefusesAMalformedCount' && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietRefusesBeforeItTouchesTheEnvironment' && printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestQuietRefusesNoSystem'

behavior: The internal/cmd test binary starts and exits cleanly under the harness environment that used to abort it at TestMain. The claim is startup, not the whole suite: a host with a global core.hooksPath runs a full hook chain on every fixture commit, which pushes the suite past Go's per-binary timeout, so CI owns the full run.
verification: cd cli && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.interactive GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=never GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=core.fsmonitor GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=false go test ./internal/cmd -run '^$' -count=1
